title: Martyrs break the power of demons
source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ αἱ ψυχαὶ τῶν διὰ χριστιανισμὸν ἀποθνῃσκόντων δι᾿ εὐσέβειαν μετ᾿ εὐκλείας ἀπαλλαττόμεναι τοῦ σώματος καθῄρουν τὴν δύναμιν τῶν δαιμόνων καὶ ἀτονωτέραν αὐτῶν ἐποίουν τὴν κατὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπιβουλὴν, διὰ τοῦτο οἶμαι τῇ πείρᾳ μαθόντες οἱ δαίμονες ἑαυτοὺς ἡττωμένους καὶ κρατουμένους ὑπὸ τῶν μαρτύρων τῆς ἀληθείας ἐφοβήθησαν πάλιν ἥκειν ἐπὶ τὸ ἀμύνεσθαι· καὶ οὕτως, ἕως ἐπιλάθωνται ὧν πεπόνθασι πόνων, εἰκὸς εἶναι τὴν τοῦ κόσμου πρὸς Χριστιανοὺς εἰρήνην. ἐπὰν δὲ συλλέξωνται τὴν δύναμιν καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς κακίας τυφλούμενοι πάλιν ἀμύνεσθαι θέλωσι καὶ Χριστιανοὺς διώκειν, πάλιν καθαιρεθήσονται· καὶ τότε πάλιν αἱ ψυχαὶ τῶν εὐσεβούντων καὶ δι᾿ εὐσέβειαν ἀποδυομένων τὰ σώματα καθελοῦσι τὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ στρατόπεδον. ἐγὼ δ᾿ οἶμαι ὅτι αἰσθόμενοι οἱ δαίμονες ὅτι οἱ μὲν νικῶντες καὶ δι᾿ εὐσέβειαν ἀποθνῄσκοντες καθαιροῦσιν αὐτῶν τὴν δυναστείαν οἱ δὲ διὰ τοὺς πόνους ἡττώμενοι καὶ τὴν θεοσέβειαν ἀρνούμενοι ὑποχείριοι ἐκείνοις γίνονται, ἔσθ᾿ ὅτε προσφιλονεικοῦσι τοῖς παραδιδομένοις Χριστιανοῖς, ὡς κολαζόμενοι μὲν ὑπὸ τῆς ὁμολογίας αὐτῶν ἀναπαυόμενοι δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ ἀρνήσει αὐτῶν. καὶ ἔστιν γε τούτων ἴχνη θεάσασθαι καὶ ἐν τοῖς δικασταῖς, κολαζομένοις μὲν ὑπὸ τοῖς ὑπομένουσι τὰς αἰκίας καὶ τὰς βασάνους γαυρουμένοις δὲ, ὅταν Χριστιανὸς ἡττηθῇ. καὶ γὰρ οὐδὲ διὰ δοκοῦσαν αὐτοῖς φιλανθρωπίαν ταῦτα ποιοῦσι, σαφῶς ὁρῶντες ὅτι „ἡ“ μὲν „γλῶσσα“ τῶν νικωμένων ὑπὸ πόνου ὀμώμοκεν, „ἡ δὲ φρήν“ ἐστιν „ἀνώμοτος“ καὶ ταῦτα δ᾿ εἰς τὸ ἀλλ᾿ οὗτοί γε καὶ σφόδρα ἀμύνονται τὸν βλασφημοῦντα, ἤτοι φεύγοντα διὰ τοῦτο καὶ κρυπτόμενον ἢ ἁλισκόμενον καὶ ἀπολλύμενον. κἂν φεύγῃ δέ τις Χριστιανὸς, οὐ διὰ δειλίαν φεύγει. ἀλλὰ τηρῶν ἐντολὴν τοῦ διδασκάλου καὶ ἑαυτὸν φυλάττων καθαρὸν ἑτέρων ὠφεληθησομένων σωτηρίᾳ.
pass_a_gloss: But since the souls of those dying on account of Christianity (χριστιανισμόν) through piety (εὐσέβειαν), departing (ἀπαλλαττόμεναι) the body with glory (εὐκλείας), were pulling down (καθῄρουν) the power (δύναμιν) of the demons and making their plotting (ἐπιβουλήν) against men feebler (ἀτονωτέραν), for this reason I think (οἶμαι) the demons, having learned by trial (πείρᾳ) that they were being defeated (ἡττωμένους) and mastered (κρατουμένους) by the martyrs (μαρτύρων) of the truth, feared (ἐφοβήθησαν) to come again to avenging themselves (ἀμύνεσθαι); and thus, until they forget the pains (πόνων) they suffered, it is likely (εἰκός) that the peace (εἰρήνην) of the world toward Christians exists. But whenever they gather (συλλέξωνται) their power and, blinded (τυφλούμενοι) by wickedness, wish again to avenge themselves and to persecute (διώκειν) Christians, they will again be pulled down; and then again the souls of those being pious (εὐσεβούντων) and through piety stripping off (ἀποδυομένων) their bodies will pull down the camp/army (στρατόπεδον) of the evil one (τοῦ πονηροῦ). And I think that the demons, perceiving (αἰσθόμενοι) that those conquering (νικῶντες) and dying through piety pull down their dominion (δυναστείαν), while those defeated by the pains and denying (ἀρνούμενοι) their reverence for God (θεοσέβειαν) become subject (ὑποχείριοι) to them, sometimes contend obstinately (προσφιλονεικοῦσι) against the Christians being handed over (παραδιδομένοις), as being punished/tormented (κολαζόμενοι) by their confession (ὁμολογίας) but resting (ἀναπαυόμενοι) at their denial (ἀρνήσει). And it is possible to behold traces (ἴχνη) of these things also in the judges (δικασταῖς), tormented by those enduring the outrages (αἰκίας) and the tortures (βασάνους), but exulting (γαυρουμένοις) whenever a Christian is defeated. For not even through seeming humanity (φιλανθρωπίαν) do they do these things, clearly seeing that the tongue (γλῶσσα) of those overcome by pain has sworn (ὀμώμοκεν), but the mind (φρήν) is unsworn (ἀνώμοτος). And these things also with reference to: 'but these vigorously avenge themselves on the blasphemer, who either flees for this reason and hides, or is caught and perishes'. And if a Christian flees, he does not flee through cowardice (δειλίαν), but keeping (τηρῶν) the command (ἐντολήν) of the Teacher (διδασκάλου) and guarding (φυλάττων) himself pure (καθαρόν) for the salvation (σωτηρίᾳ) of others who will be benefited (ὠφεληθησομένων).
pass_b_english: But the souls of those who die for Christianity out of piety, leaving the body with glory, were pulling down the power of the demons and weakening their plots against mankind. That, I think, is why the demons, having learned by experience that they were being defeated and overcome by the martyrs of the truth, were afraid to return to taking vengeance. And so, until they forget the pains they have suffered, the world is likely to be at peace with Christians. But when they gather their strength, and, blinded by wickedness, wish again to take vengeance and to persecute Christians, they will be pulled down again; and then once more the souls of the godly, who for piety’s sake put off their bodies, will pull down the army of the evil one.

For my part I think that the demons, perceiving that those who conquer and die for piety pull down their dominion, while those who are overcome by the pains and deny their reverence for God become subject to them, sometimes strive hard against the Christians who are handed over, as though they were tormented by their confession and relieved by their denial. Traces of this may be seen in the judges too, who are tormented by those who endure the outrages and the tortures, but exult whenever a Christian is defeated. Nor is it out of the kindness they seem to have that they do this, since they see plainly that the “tongue” of those overcome by pain “has sworn, but the mind” is “unsworn” (Euripides, Hippolytus 612).

This too in reply to his words: “But these at least take vigorous vengeance on the one who blasphemes them, so that he either flees for this reason and hides, or is caught and perishes.” Even if a Christian flees, he does not flee from cowardice, but in keeping with the command of his Teacher (Matthew 10:23), and he keeps himself pure for the salvation of others who are yet to be helped.

choices.choice: The opening Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεί (‘But since’) is one long sentence; English splits it as ‘But the souls ... were pulling down ... That, I think, is why the demons ... were afraid’, which keeps ‘I think’ (οἶμαι) on the main claim and ‘having learned’ as the participle it is. μαρτύρων is rendered ‘martyrs’, which also keeps its sense of ‘witnesses’ to the truth. κολαζομένοις μὲν ὑπὸ τοῖς ὑπομένουσι is faulty Greek (ὑπό with a dative where ‘by those who endure’ is meant; perhaps read ὑπὸ τῶν ὑπομενόντων or ἐπὶ τοῖς ὑπομένουσι); rendered ‘tormented by those who endure’, which gives the same sense either way. The line about the tongue and the mind is Euripides, Hippolytus 612 (ἡ γλῶσσ᾿ ὀμώμοχ᾿, ἡ δὲ φρὴν ἀνώμοτος), a well-known saying; Origen means that the judges know a forced denial is not a real one. καὶ ταῦτα δ᾿ εἰς τό ... has no verb; rendered ‘This too in reply to his words’. ‘The command of his Teacher’ is the command to flee persecution, Matthew 10:23 (‘When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next’); no words are quoted, but the reference is clear, so it is cited. ‘Put off their bodies’ (ἀποδυομένων τὰ σώματα) may echo 2 Corinthians 5:4; not cited. διὰ δοκοῦσαν αὐτοῖς φιλανθρωπίαν is rendered ‘out of the kindness they seem to have’.

First sentence restructured: 'For this reason, I think, the demons learned ... and were afraid' made 'learned' a main verb; now 'That, I think, is why the demons, having learned by experience ..., were afraid to return to taking vengeance' (πάλιν ἥκειν: 'return', dropping the doubled 'come back again')
Second sentence: 'I think that the demons perceive ... So they sometimes strive' put 'I think' on the wrong verb; now 'I think that the demons, perceiving ..., sometimes strive hard'
ἡττώμενοι: 'worn down' changed to 'overcome'; 'as though they are tormented' changed to 'were'
διὰ δοκοῦσαν αὐτοῖς φιλανθρωπίαν: unclear 'out of what seems to them kindness either' changed to 'Nor is it out of the kindness they seem to have'
Checked: Euripides, Hippolytus 612 (ἡ γλῶσσ᾿ ὀμώμοχ᾿, ἡ δὲ φρὴν ἀνώμοτος); Matthew 10:23 (flee to the next town) fits 'the command of his Teacher'
